comparison: Both evaluate baseline data claims C1-C9. OpenEval finds them well-supported by MAP and WorldPop data sources. Peer review raises UNCERTAIN evaluation due to Reviewer 3's concern that year 2000 baseline data may not be relevant for current policy decisions, suggesting 2016 baseline would be more appropriate.

Both address modeling framework claims C10-C16. OpenEval finds them SUPPORTED with acknowledgment of simplifying assumptions. Peer review also finds SUPPORTED, with Reviewers 1-2 affirming the rigorous modeling approach. OpenEval includes C17-C18 (projection results) while peer review groups these with the modeling framework.

OpenEval evaluates theoretical maximum reduction claims C17-C18 as SUPPORTED but notes they assume uniform 80% coverage. Peer review groups these projection claims with the broader modeling framework (C10-C18) and finds them SUPPORTED as part of the rigorous analysis.

Both evaluate optimization results C19-C23. OpenEval finds SUPPORTED with appropriate methodology. Peer review also finds SUPPORTED, with Reviewer 1 calling it a 'valuable finding' and Reviewer 2 noting rigorous analysis. Peer review groups additional summary claims C46-C50, C87 with these optimization results.

Both address the policy trade-off between elimination and case reduction (C24-C28). OpenEval finds SUPPORTED as internally consistent with important policy implications. Peer review also finds SUPPORTED, with reviewers acknowledging the trade-off finding. Peer review groups additional related claims C29-C31, C51-C52, C88 together.

OpenEval evaluates quantification of case burden trade-off (C29-C31, C51-C52) as SUPPORTED. Peer review groups these claims with the broader trade-off discussion (C24-C28, C88) and finds them SUPPORTED, noting the work is 'of interest from a global funder perspective.'

Both address balanced strategy claim C32. OpenEval finds SUPPORTED as a compromise approach. Peer review groups C32 with species-specific claims C33-C35, C58, C93 and finds UNCERTAIN due to Reviewer 3's concern that models don't account for interplay between species regarding immunity.

Both evaluate species-specific impact claims C33-C35, C58. OpenEval finds SUPPORTED with external validation from cited studies. Peer review finds UNCERTAIN, with Reviewer 3 concerned that not accounting for species interplay 'underplays the overall disease dynamics.' Peer review also includes C93 in this evaluation.

Both address optimal allocation patterns C36-C41, C54, C86, C89. OpenEval finds SUPPORTED as key policy-relevant findings dependent on cost assumptions. Peer review also finds SUPPORTED, implicitly accepting allocation patterns as part of the optimization results. OpenEval includes C87 while peer review includes C57.

Perfect match on sensitivity analysis claims C42-C45. Both find SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes limited scope of sensitivity analyses. Peer review does not critique the sensitivity testing approach, with Reviewer 2's statement about rigorous analysis encompassing these robustness checks.

OpenEval evaluates summary comparison claims C46-C50 as SUPPORTED, noting they are model-dependent. Peer review groups these with optimization results C19-C23, C87 and finds them SUPPORTED as part of the overall rigorous analysis providing evidence for prioritizing high-transmission settings.

OpenEval evaluates fundamental trade-off summary C88 as SUPPORTED key policy insight. Peer review groups this with broader trade-off claims C24-C31, C51-C52 and finds SUPPORTED, with reviewers acknowledging the trade-off without critique.

OpenEval evaluates citations to prior studies C53, C55-C56, C59 as SUPPORTED with appropriate external validation. Peer review groups these with extensive background claims C60-C75, C83-C85, C90-C92, C94 and finds SUPPORTED as established knowledge, not challenging the contextual claims.

OpenEval evaluates interpretive conclusions C57, C93 as SUPPORTED but appropriately qualified, noting they involve policy judgments beyond strict model demonstration. Peer review groups C93 with species-specific claims and finds UNCERTAIN due to concerns about not modeling species interplay.

OpenEval evaluates C57 as SUPPORTED interpretive conclusion. Peer review groups C57 with allocation pattern claims C36-C41, C54, C86, C89 and finds SUPPORTED as part of the optimization results providing evidence for different approaches.

Both address background/contextual claims. OpenEval evaluates C60-C75 as SUPPORTED with appropriate citations establishing study motivation. Peer review groups these with additional contextual claims C53, C55-C56, C59, C83-C85, C90-C92, C94 and finds SUPPORTED as established knowledge supporting the framing.

OpenEval evaluates ITN focus justification C76-C77 as SUPPORTED but notes single-intervention is a significant limitation. Peer review groups these with model provenance and cost claims C78-C82 and finds UNCERTAIN, with Reviewer 2 extensively listing limitations including lack of other interventions.

OpenEval evaluates model provenance claims C78-C80 as SUPPORTED, noting validation history strengthens confidence. Peer review groups these with methodological justifications C76-C77, C81-C82 and finds UNCERTAIN, with reviewers acknowledging models are 'previously published' but extensively listing limitations.

OpenEval evaluates cost assumptions C81-C82 as SUPPORTED with appropriate citations, noting sensitivity analysis shows robustness. Peer review groups these with broader methodological claims C76-C80 and finds UNCERTAIN, with extensive limitations listed including lack of other interventions and setting heterogeneity.

OpenEval evaluates funding context claims C83-C85 as SUPPORTED with appropriate citations. Peer review groups these with extensive background claims C53, C55-C56, C59-C75, C90-C92, C94 and finds SUPPORTED as established knowledge not challenged by reviewers.

OpenEval evaluates methodological definitions C90-C92 as SUPPORTED with standard definitions appropriately applied. Peer review groups these with broader contextual claims C53, C55-C56, C59-C75, C83-C85, C94 and finds SUPPORTED as established knowledge supporting study motivation.

OpenEval evaluates P. vivax limitation claim C94 as SUPPORTED, noting it appropriately acknowledges need for additional interventions beyond model scope. Peer review groups this with extensive background claims C53, C55-C56, C59-C75, C83-C85, C90-C92 and finds SUPPORTED as part of established contextual knowledge.
